Keywords: welcome onboarding new subscriber first email intro brand
Subject Line Formula: Welcome to [Brand]! Here's your first step / "You're in! Here's what happens next" / "Your [Freebie] is here"
Opening: Start with warm gratitude + what they'll get. Reference what they signed up for specifically.
Body Structure: 1. Thank them. 2. Deliver promised value (lead magnet/access). 3. Set expectations for what emails they'll receive. 4. Tell them one thing to do right now. 5. Show your personality.
CTA: Complete Your Profile / Access Your [Resource] / Start Your Free Trial
Metrics: Open rate (target 50%+), click rate, activation rate, trial starts
Best For: All email lists — this is the most important email you'll send
Segmentation: Send to all new subscribers immediately. Personalize with first name and signup source.

Keywords: sale discount offer coupon limited time flash promo promotional
Subject Line Formula: [First Name], your exclusive [X]% off expires tonight / "Last chance: [Deal] ends at midnight" / "For you only: [Offer]"
Opening: Get to the offer in the first 2 sentences. Don't bury the lead.
Body Structure: . State the offer clearly (what, how much, when it expires). 2. Show the value/savings. 3. One or two social proof elements. 4. Clear deadline. 5. Single CTA.
CTA: Shop Now / Claim My Discount / Get [X]% Off
Send Time: Tuesday-Thursday 10am or 6pm (local time). Flash sales: any time with urgency.
Metrics: Open rate, CTR, conversion rate, revenue per email, unsubscribes
Best For: E-commerce, SaaS upgrade offers, seasonal campaigns
Segmentation: Segment by: past purchasers, cart abandoners, tier (new vs loyal). Exclude recent buyers.

Keywords: newsletter content update value weekly monthly educational digest
Subject Line Formula: [Month] Digest: [Key Insight] + [Other Story] / "3 things worth your attention this week" / "What we learned about [Topic] this month"
Opening: One strong hook in the first line — a surprising stat, bold claim, or story opener.
Body Structure: 1. Main story/insight (most valuable). 2. 2-3 shorter items (articles, tips, tools). 3. Quick win or actionable takeaway. 4. Soft CTA to content or product. Keep it scannable.
CTA: Read More / Explore / Check It Out
Metrics: Open rate (aim 25-40%), CTOR, unsubscribe rate, replies (engagement signal)
Best For: B2B, content brands, SaaS, thought leaders, media
Segmentation: Send to all subscribers. Segment engagement: resend to non-openers with different subject after 3 days.

Keywords: abandoned cart recover purchase incomplete checkout ecommerce
Subject Line Formula: You left something behind, [First Name] / "Still thinking about it? Here's 10% off" / "Your [Product] is almost gone"
Opening: Reference the specific product they left. Make it feel personal, not automated.
Body Structure: 1. Name the product with image + price. 2. Remind why it's great (1-2 benefits). 3. Address common objection (returns, shipping). 4. Offer incentive if 2nd or 3rd email. 5. Create urgency (low stock).
CTA: Complete My Purchase / Save My Cart / Get 10% Off (2nd email)
Send Time: Email 1: 1 hour after abandonment. Email 2: 24 hours. Email 3: 72 hours with discount.
Metrics: Recovery rate (target 5-15%), revenue recovered, conversion rate
Segmentation: Segment: Guest vs account holder. Exclude those who purchased. Personalize with cart contents.

Keywords: reengagement winback inactive dormant lapsed churn churned cold subscribers
Subject Line Formula: We miss you, [First Name] / "Is this goodbye?" / "Here's what's changed since you left" / "A gift for coming back"
Opening: Acknowledge the gap warmly. Be human, not corporate. A touch of humor works well.
Body Structure: 1. Acknowledge they've been quiet. 2. What's new or improved since they left. 3. Special offer or free gift. 4. Ask if they want to stay (with unsubscribe option). 5. One simple ask.
CTA: Return to [Product] / Claim Your Gift / See What's New / Stay or Go (let them choose)
Send Time: Send 90 days after last engagement. Or 30 days after churn for SaaS.
Metrics: Re-activation rate, open rate, unsubscribe rate (healthy to clean list), win-back revenue
Segmentation: Target: 60/90/120-day inactive or churned customers. Don't send re-engagement to recent actives.

Keywords: drip sequence nurture onboarding education journey automated email series
Subject Line Formula: Email 1: Deliver value fast. Email 2: Story/problem. Email 3: Case study. Email 4: Offer.
Opening: Each email should feel like a conversation, not a broadcast. Reference previous emails.
Body Structure: Email sequence structure: 1. Deliver lead magnet + quick win. 2. Share your story / problem you solve. 3. Case study/result proof. 4. Objection handler. 5. Soft pitch. 6. Hard CTA with deadline.
CTA: Varies per email: Read the Case Study / Book a Demo / Start Free Trial
Send Time: Space emails 1-2 days apart. Don't overwhelm. Max 2 emails per week in nurture.
Metrics: Sequence completion rate, email-to-email open rate, conversion from sequence, reply rate
Best For: SaaS, online courses, coaching, B2B services, high-ticket offers
Segmentation: Trigger by: lead magnet download, signup source, job title (B2B), product category (e-commerce).

Keywords: launch new product feature announcement release update
Subject Line Formula: Introducing: [Product Name] / "Today's the day: [Product] is live" / "[Problem] — finally solved"
Opening: Open with the problem you're solving, not the product name.
Body Structure: : Bold announcement + product name. 2. Core benefit in one sentence. 3. Top 3 features with benefits (not features alone). 4. Early bird offer or launch discount. 5. Strong CTA.
CTA: Shop Now / Get Early Access / See the Full Launch / Claim Launch Pricing
Send Time: Send launch email on Tuesday or Wednesday at 10am. Follow up 2-3 days later to non-buyers.
Metrics: Open rate, click rate, launch day revenue, new customer rate, launch email conversion
Best For: E-commerce (new product), SaaS (new feature), creator (new course/offer)
Segmentation: Segment: VIP list first (24hr early access), then full list. Re-send to non-openers.

Keywords: transactional receipt order confirmation shipping password reset notification
Subject Line Formula: Your order is confirmed (#12345) / "Your [Product] is on the way!" / "Reset your password"
Opening: State the purpose immediately. These are expected — be clear and fast.
Body Structure: 1. Confirm the action (order/payment/reset). 2. Key details (order number, items, tracking). 3. What happens next. 4. Support contact. 5. Optional: subtle upsell or referral invite.
CTA: Track My Order / Set My Password / View My Account
Metrics: Delivery rate, click rate (on tracking links), support ticket reduction
Segmentation: These are automated and triggered per-user. No segmentation needed — send to all relevant users.

CTA: Subject line types: 1. Curiosity gap ('You won't believe...'). 2. Number ('7 email tips...'). 3. Personal ('Hey [First Name]'). 4. Direct benefit ('Double your opens in 30 days'). 5. Question ('Are you making this mistake?'). 6. Urgency ('Closes tonight').
Metrics: Always A/B test subject lines. Test on 20% of list, send winner to 80% after 4 hours.
Best For: Open rate (benchmark: 21% avg, 35%+ excellent), preview text CTR
Segmentation: All email types — subject line is the #1 factor in open rate
column11: Test subject line A/B with 20/20/60 split. Segment by engagement: dormant subscribers need punchier subjects.

Keywords: design html template mobile responsive plain text images
Opening: Open with the most important message in the first line (preview text visibility)
Body Structure: 1. One column layout (mobile-first). 2. 600px max width. 3. Large CTA button (min 44px tall). 4. Alt text on all images (many clients block images). 5. Plain text version always included. 6. Unsubscribe link required by law.
CTA: Use contrast button (not subtle). Minimum 120x44px. Use action verbs.
Metrics: Click rate, mobile open rate (60%+ of emails opened on mobile), rendering across clients
Segmentation: Send plain text version to non-HTML clients. Test rendering in Gmail, Apple Mail, Outlook before sending.
